subject: Meteorology
title: Fog Types
description: A fast breakdown of Fog Types for builders.

hook.text: Fog is simply a cloud at ground level—but for aviation, it's one of the most frequent causes of delay and danger.

buildup.text: Radiation fog forms on clear, calm nights—the ground cools the air until moisture condenses into a ground-hugging cloud.

discovery.text: Advection fog forms when warm, moist air flows over cold surfaces—common along coastlines and over cold ocean currents.

twist.text: Fog can cut visibility to zero in minutes—forcing diversions even when the destination was clear an hour earlier.

climax.text: San Francisco's fog is advection fog—warm Pacific air hits the cold California Current, creating its famous blanket.

punchline.text: A cloud on the ground—and flights grind to a halt.

quiz.question: How does radiation fog form?
options: Warm air flows over cold water
